Updated: 10:12 AM EST Nov 27, 2026

BOSTON —

One retailer's plan to welcome Black Friday shoppers was derailed when a car drove through the front window of the shop in Boston's Jamaica Plain neighborhood.

NewsCenter 5 went to 315 Centre Street and saw that a Toyota RAV4 had crashed into the Rainbow Shops location there. The vehicle had traveled about 10 feet into the store. 

District 9 Chief Joseph Walsh said the crash was reported at 8:32 a.m. 

According to the clothing retailer's website, the store was scheduled to open at 10 a.m. 

"As you can see, there's a large hole in the building," Walsh said. 

Walsh said the driver of the vehicle was uninjured and the vehicle itself was largely undamaged. One woman, who was inside preparing to open the store, was not near the front window at the time of the crash. 

A daycare facility located under the store was not in operation Friday because of the holiday. 

"Right now we're turning the building over to management. The police will be on scene for the next few hours, I'm sure, waiting for it to be boarded up and secured," Walsh said.
